Region and Spell
Automation.

More spellcraft. Less micromanagement.

Persistent Regions, attacks, damage, effects, and weapon masteries—working through the D&D5e activities and chat cards you already use. Cast spells, use features, and attack normally; choose the automation that suits your table.

Feature summaryHow to useBehind the scenes
New in v0.6.1

More attacks.
One connected workflow.

Keep using native activities and damage cards. New helpers connect repeat attacks, configured bonus damage, and corrections without replacing your attack system.

  • Eldritch Blast & Scorching Ray: a Pending Attacks window tracks remaining shots at the character or cast level. Choose targets between shots without spending another slot; canceled attacks do not consume a shot.
  • Bonus damage riders: Hex, Hunter's Mark, and Conjure Minor Elementals add optional components to the existing attack damage card. Sneak Attack uses your feature's configured damage with a once-per-combat-turn marker.
  • Attack property assistance: Savage Attacker rolls two complete weapon dice sets and keeps the higher total. Reckless Attack works through the native Strength attack and the character's feature effect.
  • Clear corrections: applied damage locks attack/save mode and Normal/Critical adjustments. Undo Damage first, correct the roll, then apply again.
  • Reaction and save support: manual off-turn uses are tracked as reactions, and a GM or token owner can take over a pending save.

Less repetition at the table

From the spell
to the finishing blow.

Your existing items, activities, rolls, and cards stay at the center. The module builds on native D&D5e workflows, rather than creating a replacement attack system over the top of them.

I.Make the area matter

Persistent Region effects

Built from the spells themselves. Configured by the GM. Connected to the area your player places.

Use a spell's own activities to trigger events when creatures enter, exit, or move through its Region, or start and end their turns inside it. A natural fit for ongoing areas such as Spirit Guardians and Hunger of Hadar.

  • Make it your own. Configure custom or prebuilt spells with matching activities and the events your table needs. The module automatically attaches that configuration to the Region created by the player's cast.
  • Let effects follow the area. Add conditions or existing spell Active Effects to apply to creatures inside the Region and remove the Region's effects when they leave.
  • One turn, one shared spell card. Enable Share Activity Card Per Turn alongside Once Per Turn. Cast Spirit Guardians, then move through four or five different NPCs: newly affected creatures join the same card for saves and damage, while each creature triggers at most once that combat turn. When the cast and trigger use the same activity, they can share the initial cast card.
  • Add targets after the damage roll. New creatures are also added to linked damage cards, reusing the damage already rolled. The target list grows as you move, even if creatures later leave the area. Each creature still resolves its own save. Apply damage manually or enable automatic application for eligible new targets. A new combat turn starts a fresh card.
  • Count the movement for you. For spells such as Spike Growth, Movement Damage tracks distance in configured increments and builds a pending damage total. Roll from the card when ready, with GM + and − controls for adjustments.
Enter · Exit · Move within · Turn start · Turn end

II.Keep the cast connected

Regions, targeting
& concentration

Choose who is affected, correct the card, and clear the area when its job is done.

  • Auto-target according to the spell card. When you place the area, automatic targeting follows the spell card's target setting—such as enemies, allies, or everyone—to select eligible creatures inside it. Enemy and ally selection is relative to the caster. If the card does not specify enemies or allies, the module uses a matching configured Region trigger's targeting mode when available; otherwise it selects everyone eligible in the area. A confirmation step lets you add or remove targets before confirming the activity card's target list and proceeding to saves and damage.
  • Fix targets from the chat card. Use Retarget to replace the card's recorded targets with your current selection. Correct an accidental inclusion, add someone missed, or clear the list without recasting.
  • Let concentration handle cleanup. Regions linked to the originating spell are removed automatically when concentration ends. A marker on the token's right-click HUD gives the GM or actor owner a quick way to end concentration.
  • Clear instantaneous areas. Instantaneous spell and feature Regions, such as Fireball, are removed when the caster's combat turn ends. Saves and damage cards remain available.
Place → Confirm targets → Resolve → Clean up

How to use this feature →

III.A smoother save

Improved saving throws

Remembered advantage a moment too late? The original roll still counts.

Automatically prompt the affected creature's connected owner for saving throws when casting spells or features that use a Save activity. NPCs and creatures without a connected player owner fall back to the active GM.

  • Adjust after the roll. Hover over a completed saving throw to choose ADV / NORMAL / DISADV. Switch modes without starting the save over.
  • Keep the original dice. The original d20 and bonus dice are retained. An extra d20 is rolled only if needed, then cached for later mode changes, preserving the original roll and its order.
  • Keep the result connected. The save total and success or failure update on the linked cards. Damage already applied is not undone.
“Forgot that save should have had advantage?”Choose ADV. Keep your original roll.

How to use this feature →

IV.New in v0.6.1

Attacks, damage
& effects

Your weapons, spells, and features. Their existing activities. Fewer steps between the roll and the result.

  • Keep the native workflow. Use your existing D&D5e attack activities and chat cards. On a confirmed hit, the module can open the native damage dialog with critical-hit, weapon-mode, resource, and upcast information retained. Save activities with damage can prompt their native damage dialog too.
  • Choose automatic damage application. With an active GM and Auto Apply Damage enabled, attack damage applies to confirmed hit targets; save damage waits for all eligible targets to resolve their saves. Native save multipliers, resistance, vulnerability, and immunity remain in use.
  • Use the effects already on your activities. Optional automation applies configured utility buffs, effects after saves, and assigned effects on attack hits. Native application handles duration, concentration, and scaling. Configure the effect on the activity first—the module does not invent it for you.
  • Correct the roll from its card. Adjust attack advantage or disadvantage while retaining the original dice. Damage cards offer Normal/Critical corrections for supported formulas. Retarget can refresh hit results after an AC change; changing rolls does not undo damage already applied.
  • Keep corrections in reach. GM Undo Damage and Undo Effect controls reverse tracked applications from the card. Optional card simplification reduces clutter while preserving messages, dice, and history.
Existing activity → Native card → Resolve → Apply

How to use this feature →

V.New in v0.6.1

Weapon masteries

Built around the mastery unlocked on your actor and used by the weapon's native attack.

  • Sap & Vex. Sap applies on a hit and defaults the victim's next attack to disadvantage. Vex applies after damage and defaults the attacker's next attack against that same target to advantage. Card controls allow corrections.
  • Slow. Applies a non-stacking 10-foot speed reduction after damage, lasting until the source's next turn starts.
  • Topple. A hit-only card action prompts the defender's owner—or the GM for NPCs—for a Constitution save, applying a source-tracked Prone effect on failure.
  • Graze. A miss-only action creates a flat damage card using the attack's ability modifier and weapon damage type. HP application follows your damage workflow.

Enable Weapon Masteries in Module Options and keep an active GM connected. The actor must have the mastery unlocked in D&D5e's native configuration. Push, Nick, and Cleave remain manual.

Sap · Vex · Slow · Topple · Graze
